done_when: When GitHub answers with a rate-limit error, close, merge and land wait until the reset time GitHub reports (with one line saying so) and then continue, instead of stopping; new and existing repos get it on upgrade

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - the GraphQL quota is exhausted while REST has a different reset time.
The owner-approved item is: “When GitHub answers with a rate-limit error, close, merge and land wait until the reset time GitHub reports (with one line saying so) and then continue, instead of stopping; new and existing repos get it on upgrade”.
The fallback chooses GraphQL only when the error text contains “graphql”. New evidence relative to the ruling is that [gh’s own GraphQL error handling](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/v2.83.2/pkg/cmd/api/api_test.go#L490-L503) prints the error message and JSON without that prefix. `forge land --all` reaches such a `gh api graphql` call through `src/forge/land.py:374` and `src/forge/board_facts.py:102`; close’s history rebuild also calls it at `src/forge/backfill.py:38`. For a headerless refusal, this code chooses the unrelated core reset, so it can retry before GraphQL resets or wait past the reported GraphQL reset.
findings.title: Not done: When GitHub answers with a rate-limit error, close, merge and land wait until the reset time GitHub reports

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - concurrent close, merge or land requests encounter a secondary GitHub rate limit.
New evidence relative to the ruling is that [GitHub documents](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api) a separate `Retry-After` for secondary limits and says the quota endpoint can itself be subject to that limit. This code ignores `Retry-After` and uses the primary quota’s reset even when that quota still has capacity. It can therefore wait until an unrelated time; if the quota lookup is also throttled, it returns the original error instead of continuing. `src/forge/checks.py:622` is one close and merge path that makes these requests without exposing response headers.
findings.title: Functional: Honor the retry time for secondary limits

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a shared GitHub account reaches its limit while someone opens the board or runs `forge next`.
Adds work: preserve best-effort GitHub reads for the board and next; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 4
The wait now applies to every `gh` invocation, including optional reads. `src/forge/board.py:65` and `src/forge/nextstep.py:163` wait for those reads before returning local information; `src/forge/board_server.py:173` also waits without a deadline when there is no saved snapshot. Previously those paths could use their unavailable-data or cached-data behavior. They now hang until the reset, and an existing board snapshot cannot refresh local changes during that wait.
findings.title: Functional: Keep board and next responsive while GitHub is rate-limited

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - an agent runs `forge merge` for a rate-limit fix before its pull request exists.
Adds work: distinguish quota refusals from unrelated errors; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 4
`src/forge/merge.py:65` asks `gh pr view` before deciding that the item is not ready. For a branch such as `fix/rate-limit-waits`, [gh reports](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/v2.83.2/pkg/cmd/pr/shared/finder.go#L405-L413) that no pull request was found for that branch. The broad match treats the branch name as a rate-limit error, reads a normal quota reset and repeatedly waits and retries instead of returning the not-ready refusal.
findings.title: Functional: A branch name can trigger a false rate-limit wait

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - GitHub’s response header and quota endpoint report different reset times.
In both header cases the fixture gives `core.reset` the same value as the header, so the entire test still passes if production code ignores the header and always uses the quota endpoint. The GraphQL case also injects a `GraphQL:` prefix into a `pr view` error, leaving the headerless `gh api graphql` failure described above untested. Finally, line 58 checks only the announcement’s prefix, so an incorrect displayed reset time passes. The named proof therefore does not protect all the reset-source and announcement behavior it claims.
